_comment: Example config for tools/plot_sequence_eval.py (sequence-eval success by
task position, as bars).   Schema: tools/plot_common.py.
python tools/plot_sequence_eval.py --config tools/plot_sequence_example.json
Paths point at a STANDALONE EVAL's glob dir -- the one holding
eval_per_trial.csv -- not at the training run. scripts/eval.sh puts it
next to the checkpoint it evaluates:
<TRAIN_RUN>/wandb/run-<ts>-<id>/eval/wandb/run-<ts2>-<id2>/glob
(or under $RUN_OUT_DIR when that is set). Training glob dirs have no
eval_per_trial.csv and are skipped with a [warn].
Each entry in `groups` is one bar colour; in-domain bars are filled,
out-of-domain bars hollow. Each entry in a group's `runs` is one series
(typically the eval of one seed's checkpoint); the error bar is +-1 std
across them. A `runs` entry that is a LIST is several round shards of ONE
eval (e.g. --eval-rounds 0-2 and 3-5 run on two GPUs), pooled into one
series -- or merge them first with tools/rebuild_eval_outputs.py.
Writes to `out_dir` (empty = next to this file):
<name>_seq_position.png                     pooled over every task
<name>_seq_position_per_task/...            one PNG per task
<name>_seq_position.csv                     every plotted number
metric:   success (each task on its own) | success_chained | grasp | obj_grasped
seq_kind: all | training (the trained rotations) | random (untrained cycles)
Both can be overridden on the command line (--metric, --seq-kind).
Any top-level key starting with '_' is ignored, so this block can stay.
name: seq_eval_T2560
